newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen down amid flat trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen down amid flat trend.

text.p: Polish shares eased in higher turnover on Tuesday and analysts expected them to fall further on profit taking on Wednesday but to remain within their 2.5-month long horizontal trend.
The main market's WIG index fell 0.1 percent, to 16,170.3, and turnover rose 13.8 percent to 153.1 million zlotys ($47.8 million) on all three markets as 30 issues fell, 36 rose and 28 were flat.
Analysts said local speculators, the main driving force during a relatively quiet period, pushed shares lower taking profits after a recent round of bottom-fishing.
"Investors buy what they think is cheap, and when it rises they sell it, it's a short-term play for growth or falls," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria brokerage.
The bourse rose 2.7 percent from last Wednesday to Monday, after it fell 4.5 percent in the previous four sessions.

Analysts said the rapid movements of the bourse within a broad channel of 15,500 and 17,000 were possible because of low turnovers and were likely to be maintained possibly until September general elections.
They said the busy primary market was also keeping investors diverted from the bourse.
Analysts said many of foreign investors were waiting on the sidelines for September parliamentary elections before taking investment decisions.

They said Bank Handlowy public offer worth about one billion zlotys ($312 million), household appliances makers Amica Wronki more than 100 million zloty ($31.3 million) offer and expected June sale of copper giant KGHM were drawing capital from the bourse.
But they said in the longer-term listing of the firms could attract additional capital to the bourse, increasing its capitalisation and liquidity.
